steps.text: Preheat a waffle iron according to manufacturer's instructions.

Whisk the flour, baking powder, sugar, and salt together in a mixing bowl; set aside. Beat egg whites until foamy in a separate large glass or metal mixing bowl. Whisk the egg yolks, lemon zest, and vanilla extract together in a third bowl; whisk in the milk. Stir in the flour mixture until smooth. Fold in the melted butter and then the beaten egg whites until just incorporated.
Cook the waffles according to manufacturer's instructions until golden brown.

review.reviewBody: I've tried so many waffle recipes and thought many of them were really good, but this one- WOW! These are the yummiest waffles I've EVER had-soft, but slightly crunchy, super fluffy, and with just the right amount of sweetness. I didn't add the lemon zest (no lemons) and thought I had messed it up, as I ran out of milk and had to leave everything to run to the store. But they still came out perfect. You have to try these!

Not awful if chewy is what u want. Made exact then adjusted twice more... final result was same ingredients, 2 whipped eggs in magic bullet and fold into everything else as stated in recipe. U dont need the 2 extra yolks which weigh it down. U could also do 4 tbsp of butter instead of 6. Third time i added brown sugar instead of white and doubled vanilla. These changes in 3rd attempt produced a light fluffy non chewy waffle with subtle hint of vanilla that went well with syrup, whipped cream and berries. Sometimes less is more. Also wasnt into the lemon zest. I love lemon but in this recipe it wasnt for me.

This was the first time making waffles, and the batter was extremely easy/quick to make. 

I reduced the butter to two tablespoons to reduce the amount of fat. The waffles still came out perfect. 

Also, instead of lemon zest, I used about a tablespoon of lemon juice. It added just the right amount of "sour" to the batter to complement the salt and sugar.
Turned out great. Added 4 T sugar snd 1/2t of almond extract. Crispy outside with a moist, chewy inside. Definitely my new “go to” for waffles!
This was a great recipe! I did however add 1 whole tsp of salt instead of 1/2, and use lime zest instead of lemon. They were perfect, my family was ooo'ing and aaah'ing.

Great for our family! I scooped cherry pie filling over mine, my child says "he's just not into cherry". Made 7 total. I cooled extras on a rack so the bottom wouldn't soften and will freeze them in a plastic bag.

I loved this recipe. I ran out of milk so I used a combination of 2% Lactaid- about 3/4c, 1/2c whole milk and 1/4c heavy cream. We had oranges on hand so I used orange zest instead. YUM- YUM!!
Very easy to make- and the list of dry ingredients separated from the wet helped me be more aware of the steps.

a couple of weeks ago I was looking for a tasty and easy waffle recipe, I found one from this website but I did not save it and when I checked again today I could not find it. given the high number of reviews and high rating this recipe got I decided to make this instead-I am happy I did. 
to make the waffles healthier I replaced one cup of white flour with 1 cup of whole wheat flour. as expected this made the batter thicker and the waffles were not as thin as they would be with just white flour. I also did not add lemon zest and increased vanilla by a 1/4 tsp--they tasted great. I am giving this recipe 4 star just because of the number of steps involved in making the batter.

This is our go to recipe for waffles. We make a double batch on New Years Day to serve sleepover party guests. It doubles well!

I almost never add the lemon zest, it is great without it. Otherwise I make it as described. 

I also tend to add extras for flavoured waffles. I have added chocolate chips, pecans, butterscotch chips, walnuts, the lost goes on, the batter worked well with everything.

One last note. When everyone is full, I use the remaining batter and freeze the prepared waffles . They reheat easily in the toaster and are just as delicious later!
These are so good, I added a little cornstarch for crispness and added more flour to make them Belgium style. The kids devoured them. I don't like waffles and I loved every bite.

Wow! These definitely were easy and tasted great!I cut back on the milk a bit and used buttermilk vs. whole milk. They were crispy on the outside and tender on the inside. This recipe is perfect as-is, but if you want a sweeter waffle you can up the sugar to as much as you like. I upped it to about 4-6 Tbsp and was liberal with the vanilla. These are delicious topped with real maple syrup!

Yeah yeah yeah, it's great BUT this is NOT, I repeat, NOT an "easy" recipe!!! That being said, we enjoyed them a lot. Our little waffle maker cranked out 8 waffles, so I'm more than happy to have more tomorrow morning!
I added malted milk-about 1/3 cup.
There are not a lot of tastes
No changes made. Perfect as is!!!
The lemon zest adds zing. A stand-up mixer makes this recipe easy-peasy.

Perfect waffles on the first try! I bought a waffle iron years ago, but I was so disappointed in the waffles I made (from a mix) that it's been sitting in a cabinet forgotten. Obviously I decided to give it another try, and these hit the spot! They're crisp and fluffy with just the right amount of subtle sweetness. I left out the lemon zest because I didn't have any (I'll try that another time), but I did everything else by-the-book and they were delicious as-is! My waffle iron may never go back in the cabinet!

These were easy and delicious. I had all of the ingredients needed in my pantry/fridge and it didn't require the wait time necessary for yeast-based waffles. These tasted like waffles - not pancakes - and the lemon zest really made a difference. I just used the zest from one large lemon and it was more than enough. It does require you to dirty a lot of bowls, but it was worth it.
Awesome.
We love these waffles! Texture is just what I was looking for, they're perfect!
